$comment: Which changed paths make each pull-request workflow do its work (root ADR-0201). The ONE place an area's inputs are written: workflows carry no `paths:` filter. A scoped workflow always starts and its required/* context always reports; its `scope` job runs scripts/ci/change_scope.py, and an untouched area finishes green in seconds. Implicit inputs, never listed here: the workflow file itself, every repository file the workflow names (scripts, contracts), and the selector and this file (those two run everything). `merge_group`: `full` reruns the whole workflow in the merge queue as a backstop for an input this list misses; `scoped` trusts the list there too. `unscoped` workflows always run in full, each with the reason.

unscoped.docs.yml: A link fix in one area can break a link in another, and the generated documents read every area; the whole job takes about two minutes.
unscoped.secret-scan.yml: A secret can arrive in any path; scanning every change is the point of the check.
unscoped.monorepo-guard.yml: Repository-wide invariants (layout, versions, workflow policy, supply chain) read every area.
unscoped.foundation-ci.yml: Selects its own heavy gates per job with scripts/ci/foundation_ci_scope.py; adopting this area scope there is a separate change to jobs another change is reshaping.
